root_cause: ContactChat is not keyed by peer and kept unacked own sends only in component state: after a thread switch the previous conversation's rows stayed rendered until the new thread's read resolved, and the thread-open seed (or a remount through the contact list) dropped an own send still awaiting its relay ack, since own DMs are stored only after the ack. Underneath, a delete/edit of such an unacked send was only buffered and never applied once the send was stored.
fix: ChatBox, reactions and messagesRef get only the open thread's rows (messagesForThread). New module-scope, per-account registry app/src/lib/pendingOwnSends.ts holds unacked own sends (register/replace for the image id swap/settle), tracks edits and hides of them with change notifications, and holds a settle while an edit/delete of the send is publishing. Every storage refresh in ContactChat lays the pending views over the merged rows (overlayPendingSends, also inside seedThreadMessages); settle events let a remounted view drop failed/replaced rows and re-read storage. persistOwnSend stores an acked own send and resolves delete/edit signals buffered for it.

tests_added.kinds: Pure helpers (messagesForThread, seedThreadMessages overlay, overlayPendingSends incl. two-send interleaving and image id swap, applyPendingSendChange, swapOptimisticImageRow compose tests); registry lifecycle (accounts, settle notifications, held settle with overlapping actions, aliases, change events); persistOwnSend against the idb mock (buffered delete -> tombstone, buffered edit -> content; fails without the resolve). Gap (accepted, no-jsdom convention): the ContactChat effect/handler wiring itself.

retrospective.harder_than_needed: The bug report assumed thread switches keep ContactChat mounted; the common path (contact list) remounts it, which turned a ref fix into a module-scope registry and six review rounds of concurrency cases (remount, held settles, image id swap, overlapping refreshes).
retrospective.surprised_by: A delete or edit of an unacked own DM was never applied to storage at all (buffered, then no echo ever resolved it); and deleting an uploading image cannot stick (temp id) — filed as deleting-dm-image-while-still-uploading.
